Lesson 3 of 10 in *Vital, step by step*: everything you need to feel at home in the real Vital plug-in. Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Learn what a filter does and what cutoff and resonance mean.
2. Hear 12 dB and 24 dB, low-pass, band-pass and high-pass.
3. Add drive and key tracking.
4. Learn the real Vital's two filters and how the oscillators get into them.
5. Check yourself.
:::

## What a filter does

- A **filter** takes away part of the sound. Most often it takes away the high, bright part, like putting your hand over your mouth while you sing.
- **Cutoff** is where it starts cutting. Low cutoff = dark and muffled; high cutoff = bright. In Vital it runs from 8 to 136, in semitones (piano keys) (Vital source, synth_parameters.cpp).
- **Resonance** boosts the sound right at the cutoff. A little sounds sharper; a lot makes a whistling ring.

## Model and style

- The **model** is the kind of filter circuit it copies; the **style** is how steep it cuts. The real Vital shows them together as *Model : Style*, for example **Analog : 12dB** (Vital source, filter_section.cpp).
- **12dB** cuts gently, **24dB** cuts more steeply (darker, more "synth").
- This page plays three models (Analog, Ladder, Digital) and three styles (12dB, 24dB, Notch) with its own filter code, not Vital's.

## Blend, drive, key track

- **Blend** (0 to 2) moves the filter between keeping the lows, the middle and the highs. On this page 0 = low-pass (keeps lows), 1 = band-pass (keeps a middle band), 2 = high-pass (keeps highs): this site's reading of Vital's code (unverified).
- **Drive** (0 to 20 dB) pushes the sound harder into the filter, for grit (Vital source, synth_parameters.cpp).
- **Key track** (KEY TRK) moves the cutoff with the note you play, so high notes stay as bright as low ones.

## Step by step

Each step loads a starting patch made on this page (not one of Vital's presets) and plays it. Listen for the one thing it names, then turn the knob it names.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;cut&quot;:60,&quot;res&quot;:10}" data-page="voice"><p><b>Cutoff down.</b> The saw with <b>CUTOFF</b> at 60. Listen: muffled. Drag CUTOFF slowly up to 120 while you play: the sound opens up.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;cut&quot;:70,&quot;res&quot;:70}" data-page="voice"><p><b>Resonance up.</b> <b>CUTOFF</b> 70, <b>RESONANCE</b> 70 %. Listen for the whistle on top of each note. Now move CUTOFF: the whistle moves with it.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;cut&quot;:75,&quot;res&quot;:30,&quot;fModel&quot;:&quot;Ladder&quot;,&quot;fStyle&quot;:&quot;24dB&quot;}" data-page="voice"><p><b>24 dB Ladder.</b> The style is <b>24dB</b>, the model <b>Ladder</b>, cutoff 75. Listen: darker and rounder than 12 dB. Switch the style back to 12dB to compare.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;fBlend&quot;:1,&quot;cut&quot;:80,&quot;res&quot;:30}" data-page="voice"><p><b>Blend.</b> <b>BLEND</b> at 1 (band-pass), cutoff 80: the lows and highs are gone, a nasal middle is left. Turn BLEND to 2: now only the highs, thin and fizzy.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;drive&quot;:12,&quot;cut&quot;:85,&quot;res&quot;:40}" data-page="voice"><p><b>Drive.</b> <b>DRIVE</b> 12 dB with some resonance. Listen for grit and a louder, rougher tone. Turn DRIVE to 0 to compare.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;key&quot;:100,&quot;cut&quot;:66,&quot;res&quot;:20}" data-page="voice"><p><b>Key track.</b> <b>KEY TRK</b> 100 %, cutoff 66. The melody's high notes stay bright. Set KEY TRK to 0 and play high and low keys: now the high notes go dull.</p></div>
```

## In the real Vital

What is different in the plug-in and exactly where to find it. Every line names the file of Vital's source code (github.com/mtytel/vital) it was read from; "(unverified)" means it was not confirmed.

- **Two filters.** FILTER 1 and FILTER 2 on the VOICE tab, plus a FILTER effect on the EFFECTS tab (Vital source, synthesis_interface.cpp; effects_interface.cpp).
- **Off at the start.** Each filter has an **on** switch, and in a new Init Preset both are off (Vital source, synth_parameters.cpp). Switch FILTER 1 on before turning its knobs, or you will hear no change.
- **What goes in.** Under each filter are buttons **OSC1**, **OSC2**, **OSC3** and **SMP** (the sample) that choose what it filters, and **FIL2** on filter 1 (FIL1 on filter 2) to run one filter into the other (Vital source, filter_section.cpp).
- **The trap.** At the start filter 1 takes OSC 1 and filter 2 takes OSC 2 (Vital source, synth_parameters.cpp), and OSC 3 goes straight to the effects (Vital source, oscillator_section.cpp). To filter all three with Filter 1, set each oscillator's DESTINATION to *Filter 1* (Vital source, oscillator_section.cpp).
- **All the models.** Analog, Dirty, Ladder, Digital, Diode, Formant, Comb, Phaser. Analog, Dirty, Ladder and Digital have styles 12dB, 24dB, Notch Blend, Notch Spread and B/P/N; Diode has Low Shelf and Low Cut; Comb has six styles; Phaser has Positive and Negative (Vital source, synth_strings.h; filter_section.cpp). Click the MODE box: each model opens a list of its styles; the arrows step through them all (Vital source, filter_section.cpp).
- **Knobs that change.** With Comb, DRIVE becomes CUT; with Formant you get PEAK, SPREAD and an X / Y pad instead of cutoff and resonance (Vital source, filter_section.cpp). Formant's style list is not settled in the notes (unverified).
- **Starting values.** Cutoff 60, resonance 50 %, mix 100 %, Analog : 12dB (Vital source, synth_parameters.cpp). There is also a **MIX** knob (filtered against dry) and the cutoff can be shown in Hz (Vital source, filter_section.cpp).

## Try it in the real Vital

Open Vital in your DAW (see [Meet Vital](intro-vital.qmd) to install it) and do these in order.

- [ ] Initialize the preset. Switch **FILTER 1** on.
- [ ] Drag CUTOFF down and up while playing. Then raise RESONANCE.
- [ ] Click the MODE box and choose **Ladder**, then **24dB**.
- [ ] Turn OSC 2 on. Is it filtered? Check the **OSC2** button under FILTER 1, or set OSC 2's DESTINATION to Filter 1.
- [ ] Try the Comb model and listen to how different it is.
- [ ] Turn DRIVE up and listen for grit.

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Turning Cutoff down makes the sound…</b></p><ul><li>Darker and more muffled</li><li>Louder</li><li>Higher in pitch</li><li>Echo</li></ul><p class="ik-why">The filter takes away the highs above the cutoff.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What does Resonance do?</b></p><ul><li>Boosts the sound at the cutoff, up to a whistle</li><li>Adds voices</li><li>Changes the wavetable</li><li>Makes notes longer</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Step 2.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>You turn Filter 1&#x27;s cutoff in a new Init Preset and nothing changes. Why?</b></p><ul><li>The filter starts switched off</li><li>The cutoff knob is broken</li><li>You need the MATRIX tab</li><li>Filters only work on chords</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Filter on defaults to 0 (synth_parameters.cpp).</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>In the real Vital, how does OSC 2 get into Filter 1?</b></p><ul><li>The OSC2 button under Filter 1, or OSC 2's destination set to Filter 1</li><li>It always does</li><li>Through the reverb</li><li>It cannot</li></ul><p class="ik-why">filter_section.cpp input buttons; oscillator_section.cpp destination.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Which is steeper?</b></p><ul><li>24dB</li><li>12dB</li><li>They are the same</li><li>Neither cuts anything</li></ul><p class="ik-why">24 dB per octave cuts more than 12.</p></div>
```
